text:
anya: quick data point — spun up branching-sampler on quant-13b-int4 for the throughput bench. small thread with results and next steps.
ben: nice, what's the config?
anya: branch_width=2, entropy_thresh=1.2, speculative_budget=6 tokens, no kv-prefetch. used our new quick-eval harness (scripts/eval/branch_probe.py).
maggie: did you run the full hellman-suite or just lmbench?
anya: ran lmbench + 200 safety prompts from the regression set. saving raw logs to s3://redwood-experiments/branching/2714040000/.
steve: any surprising quality regressions?
anya: short summary: latency down ~22% p50, p99 down ~12%. quality tradeoff small but visible on long-form QA — answer hallucination rate up from 3.8% -> 5.6% on our metric.
ben: can you paste the eval table?
anya: ```
model,config,p50_ms,p99_ms,bleu,qa_halluc_rate
13b-fp16,baseline,180,480,31.2,3.8%
13b-int4,baseline,130,420,30.6,4.1%
13b-int4,branch-width=2,100,370,30.1,5.6%
```
maggie: interesting that fp16 baseline still higher BLEU but int4 gain in latency. Did you run with temperature variations?
anya: quick grid: temp 0.2/0.7/1.0. hallucinations increased more at higher temp as expected. branching amplifies rare-token divergence — hypothesize due to early branch committed token staleness.
steve: which metric do we prioritize for this workload (customer X search re-rank vs long-form help)?
ben: customer X cares latency >1.5x and QA quality needs to be <4% halluc. so this config fails for them. But for interactive chat it's maybe ok.
anya: canary-bot: canary run completed on dedicated pool (canary-4). 5% traffic, no errors. latency improvements match bench within 5%.
maggie: can we try hybrid: branch_width=2 but speculative_budget=3 and stronger rescore step (nucleus rescore) to reduce halluc?
anya: planning that next. also try enabling kv-prefetch and smaller micro-batches — should reduce p99 further.
ben: please add a short checklist in the PR: reproduce script, eval set, seed, full logs link, and safety check pass/fail. then we can declare experimental.
anya: will open PR with results + small runbook. tagging @ben @maggie for review. :thumbsup:
steve: note — if we see hallucation spikes on long-form, add a rollout cap in console (max 10% traffic) and auto-fallback to fp16.
anya: added to runbook. thanks all.
canary-bot: deployment note — rollout paused at 10% due to threshold rule (qa_halluc_rate > 5%).
anya: ack. pausing and iterating on rescore + smaller speculative budget.
ben: cool, update thread when you have hybrid numbers.
